senses.gloss:
Pilājī(nṛpa)
son of Keśavadāsa, patron of Śeṣakṛṣṇa (a. of Śūdrācāraśiromaṇi). See Kane, HDS. I. p. 641b.

Pilikulbhāvanā
Bud. Pāli on the components of the human body from Satipatthāna Sutta. Colombo D. I. 1323-32.

Pillaṭa
medical writer. mentioned in Cikitsāsārasaṅgraha. MD. 13145.

Pillai_Lokācārya
(1205-1326 A. D.) son of Kṛṣṇamiśra; a. important writer on South Indian Vaiṣṇavism; wrote the eighteen rahasyas in Maṇipravāla of [Page098-b] Tamil an. Sanskrit. See JBBRAS. 1910, p.. 569ff.; Poona Ori. I. 3. p. 12.
--Arthapañcaka.
Pt.. Bharati Publications. Indore, 1972.
--Tattvatraya. See Adyar D. X. 255.
--Tattvaviveka. Adyar D. X. 255. Extr. p. 278.

Pīlukācārya
writer on elephants.
Q. in Adbhutasāgara of Ballālasena, Benares edn. 1905, p.. 596. 613.
